claims.text: The conventionally processed eutectic high-entropy alloy has dual-phase lamellar colonies with internal boundaries prone to microcracking during room-temperature tensile deformation.
Adding a low, controlled concentration of Nb during processing will induce nanoscale coherent nanoprecipitates.
The Nb-induced nanoprecipitates will be uniformly distributed along the lamellar-colony interfaces.
The nanoprecipitates will impede dislocation motion.
Impeded dislocation motion will increase tensile strength.
Nanoprecipitates at colony interfaces will reinforce those interfaces and deflect or arrest microcrack initiation and propagation.
Delayed microcrack initiation and propagation will improve room-temperature tensile ductility.
Relative to the unmodified alloy, the Nb-added alloy will exhibit higher tensile strength.
Relative to the unmodified alloy, the Nb-added alloy will exhibit greater tensile ductility.
Relative to the unmodified alloy, the Nb-added alloy will show delayed microcrack formation.
The baseline eutectic high-entropy alloy has moderate strength but limited ductility because microcracks initiate early at lamellar interfaces.
The proposed benefits require an optimal low Nb concentration that produces a uniform nanoprecipitate distribution.
Excessive Nb may cause precipitate coarsening or continuous brittle layers that negate the strength and ductility benefits.
The magnitude of the strength and ductility changes will depend on nanoprecipitate size and distribution.
